verdict.rationale: uv delivers per-project package and Python pinning. Dependencies with version constraints are recorded in pyproject.toml and an exact cross-platform uv.lock, upgrades keep the rest of the lockfile intact, and `uv python pin` writes a .python-version that is then respected. Tool pinning (`uvx tool@version`, `uv tool install` honoring version specifiers and constraints on upgrade) is documented, but tools are installed globally or run in environments isolated from the project, so per-project tool pins are not shown. Missing for 10: documented per-project pinning of tools, and independent hands-on corroboration that lockfile pins are honored on sync/install.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pin exact versions of packages and tools per project and have the manager respect those pins

citations.quote: `uv.lock` is a cross-platform lockfile that contains exact information about your project's dependencies.
You can also specify version constraints or alternative sources
The `--upgrade-package` flag will attempt to update the specified package to the latest compatible version, while keeping the rest of the lockfile intact.
This will respect the Python version pinned in the project.
`uv tool install` will also respect the `{package}@{version}` and `{package}@latest` specifiers
Tool upgrades will respect the version constraints provided when installing the tool.
